prerequisites: Knowledge of high school mathematics in the range of a real gymnasium.

learning_outcomes.text: Gain an understanding of basic mathematical concepts and methods and be able to apply them in other engineering subjects.

syllabus_topics: Basics of linear algebra vectors, vector spaces, linear independence of vectors, dimensions, bases.
Matrix, operation, rank. Determinant. Regular and singular matrices, inverse matrices.
Systems of linear equations, Frobenian theorem, Gaussian elimination method.
Eigennumbers and eigenvectors of a matrix.
Differential calculus of real functions of one variable. Sequence, monotony, limit.
Limit and continuity of a function. Derivation, geometric and physical meaning.
Monotonicity of a function, local and absolute extrema, convexity, inflection point. Asymptotes, graph of the function.
Taylor polynomial, remainder after n-th power. Approximate solution of the equation f(x)=0.
Integral calculus of real functions of one variable indefinite integral, integration by parts, integration by substitution.
Application of a definite integral: surface area, volume of a rotating body, length of a curve, application in mechanics.
bibliography: Neustupa, J.: Mathematics I, CTU Publishing House, Prague, 1996
Finney, R. L., Thomas, G.B.: Calculus, Addison-Wesley, New York, Ontario, Sydney, 1994
degree: Oferta Erasmus+ en inglés de la Fac. de Ingeniería Mecánica (sin plan de grado atado)
